We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z\ge -2.15).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/f814b532742940206d119c1aa30746b128ab6ede249128e55fc949a1051220c9.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -2.15) & =1-P(Z<-2.15) \\  & =1-Φ(-2.15)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069404/assets/9e2cf363bd0732c4669c4653d83f505826af605f2bc719a4f39135d233456b57.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-2.15)=0.0158.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -2.15) & =1-Φ(-2.15) \\  & =1-0.0158 \\  & =0.9842.\end{aligned}
$$
